stem:
Ritu works in base $10$. She multiplies the landmark $100$ by $10$, then multiplies $23=20+3$ by $10$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call the answer landmark only, without moving among powers of $10$ or distributing across grouped parts.
Treat $100\times10$ as a power move to $1000$, but multiply $23\times10$ without distributing over $20+3$.
Landmark $100\times10=1000$ (power up by $1$); then $23\times10=(20+3)\times10=200+30=230$ by distributing.
Say that writing $230$ is what creates the landmark move $100\times10=1000$, instead of using power moves and distribution to build products.

teacher.key_rationale: Landmark products move among powers; multi-part factors use distribution: $100\times10=1000$ and $23\times10=230$. Naming landmark alone, skipping distribution, or reversing result and method all miss that hinge.
